content.comment_body: Our packing machine requires 24 outputs for complete operation, but a single [product_name] module cannot provide that. Is there a way to get a [product_name] logic module with more inputs and outputs soon?

Sometimes it's possible to split the task and use the last output of the first [product_name] module as an input for a second module to handle the remaining steps. However, this approach increases costs. Alternatively, you could consider another [product_name] from the [version_no] series, which could be more cost-effective depending on the machine's requirements. I've done something similar with a batching plant, using one module to manage the preparation and another for mixing, discharging, and storage. I don't expect [company_name] to increase the I/O of the [product_name] module any time soon. Good luck!
Thank you very much for your reply.

Hello I/O enthusiasts, I have looked into this issue. Even with all possible expansion modules, the software does not allow the last four digital outputs to be used in a program. This is due to the way the [product_name] reads expansion modules through its protocol and backplane bus using a specific telegram format. If [company_name] changes this format to enable more I/O, older expansion modules would no longer be compatible. The company prioritizes backward compatibility—if there's a new base module (CPU), you only need to change that piece, not all expansion modules, saving users money. The same applies to the programming cable, which is still usable across several module versions. When the [product_name] was released in 1996, USB and other standard connectors weren't available, so [company_name] designed its own cost-effective connection. For these reasons, it's unlikely that extra outputs will be added soon. Perhaps a network-capable version in the future?

Hi [user_name], an alternative solution could be the Controller XLt. You can find more information here: [url] Best regards, [user_name]. Helpful links: Collection of notes and circuits for using and programming the [product_name], scaling signals with analog blocks, and retrieving data from [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users note that the existing [product_name] logic modules, even with maximum expansion, do not provide enough outputs for complex automation needs. There is some frustration about the product's limitations, mainly due to technical constraints and a strong focus on backward compatibility. While users appreciate the long-term usability and cost savings this brings, they realize that expecting a higher-output future version is unlikely.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for a future [product_name] logic module with more digital outputs and seeks recommendations for current or upcoming options. There is a preference for solutions that enable easy system expansion and maintain backward compatibility at a reasonable cost.
